# MATH 346

Mathematical and statistical software for students who need to compute, analyze, visualize, and explain results they can defend.

This course uses MATLAB and R, with generative AI treated as a professional assistant whose output must be tested, interpreted, and documented.

::: {.pill-row}
<span class="pill">MATLAB</span>
<span class="pill">R</span>
<span class="pill">Reproducible reports</span>
<span class="pill">Numerical methods</span>
<span class="pill">Data analysis</span>
<span class="pill">AI-aware validation</span>
:::
:::

::: {.course-map}
## Course Workflow

1. Ask a precise question.
2. Choose a computational representation.
3. Write or adapt code.
4. Check the result.
5. Communicate the conclusion.
6. Document any AI assistance.
:::
:::

## Start Here

Before the first class:

1. Read the [syllabus](syllabus/index.qmd) and [AI use policy](syllabus/ai-policy.qmd).
2. Check the [software requirements](resources/software-requirements.qmd) and
   run the MATLAB setup check.
3. Open [Week 1](weeks/week-01.qmd) and its [exercise set](weeks/week-01-exercises.qmd).
4. Read the [workload guide](weeks/workload-guide.qmd): material visible on the
   site is not automatically assigned.

Weeks 1-4 and the [Quiz 1 guide](assessments/quiz-01.qmd) form the launch-ready
part of the course. Later weeks remain visible as a course roadmap and may be
refined in response to what students find difficult during the opening weeks.

## Website And Blackboard

Use this website for course explanations, weekly materials, labs, exercises,
code, project instructions, and the [glossary](resources/glossary.qmd). Use

## The Weekly Rhythm

1. Begin with the week's mathematical or statistical question.
2. Follow the selected in-class lab checkpoints.
3. Attempt the core exercises in the [workload guide](weeks/workload-guide.qmd).
4. Check your output, explain what it means, and record any AI assistance.
5. Use a [recovery checkpoint](weeks/workload-guide.qmd#phase-recovery-checkpoints)
   if an earlier phase still feels insecure.

Assessment information begins with [Quiz 1](assessments/quiz-01.qmd). Later
quiz and examination details will be published before they are needed.

## Course Question

The central question of the course is not "Can I make MATLAB or R run?"

It is:

> Can I turn a mathematical or statistical question into a reproducible computational answer that is correct, interpretable, and honestly communicated?

## Public Materials Policy

This website contains original course materials and links to references. It does not redistribute textbook PDFs, publisher slide decks, answer keys, exams, or private student work.
